verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents some event-driven automation. Guarded rollouts automatically increase traffic while monitoring metrics for regressions, webhooks send an HTTP POST when a flag changes, and an "Adaptive triggers" feature and Autopilot auto-rollback are named. None of this shows a general user-defined rule engine for mapping arbitrary events to actions; targeting rules and scheduled (time-based) changes are adjacent and not credited. Missing for 10: documentation of a configurable event→action rule builder, detail on adaptive triggers beyond a title, a documented auto-rollback trigger mechanism beyond marketing copy, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: A guarded rollout progressively increases traffic to the new variation while monitoring selected metrics for regressions until the rollout reaches 100%.
When something changes, like when a feature flag is updated... LaunchDarkly sends an HTTP POST payload to the webhook's configured URL.
Autopilot ships it safely, and rolls it back if it breaks.
